title: Test-run retention: a configurable age limit (default 7 days) for unprotected logs and detail, with a read-only preview before any cleanup
outcome: Operators can set how long positively unprotected test-run raw logs and verbose detail are kept (default 7 days, or keep indefinitely), see a read-only preview of what is protected, eligible and unknown, and only later have a bounded, restart-safe cleanup remove exactly eligible files; active, unresolved, verification-bound and evidence-cited results, compact identities and proofs are never removed.
acceptance: Slice 1 (non-destructive): a settings field for unprotected test-run log/detail retention (positive finite days, default 7, or keep indefinitely) and a read-only preview listing counts and bytes protected, eligible and unknown, with the reason per class; no file is deleted and protection semantics are unchanged. Tests cover validation, the preview classes, and that changing the setting deletes nothing.

Eligibility is measured from a trustworthy terminal endedAt; missing, future or ambiguous times, active, unresolved, pending-wait/card/notification, uncertain-ownership, verification-bound, evidence-cited and unknown-citation-coverage runs are all protected; tests cover each exemption.

Slice 2 (destructive, separately reviewed): bounded restart-safe cleanup outside StateInner, owned by the existing test-run/artifact lifecycle, that durably records the survivor identity and cleanup intent first, revalidates identity/path/terminal/protection at application, deletes only allowlisted files in the exact managed run directory, refuses links/junctions/foreign paths, reports partial deletion idempotently, and keeps a durable identity/result with an explicit log-unavailable reason; deterministic tests cover hold/deletion interleavings, crash recovery and path refusal.
Each slice: independent review pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding and the full gate on the exact committed tree.
